clue.text: Awful strain in the lead up to politician's passing

indicators.note: the jumbled piece comes ahead of the politician, placing it first
awful suggests the word strain is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone under awful strain in the run-up to a politician's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' hints at death but means fleeting. 'Awful' shuffles the fodder to TRANSI; 'in the lead up to' sets it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transitory is fleeting, merely passing through rather than lasting.

clue.text: What's the point of some animals?

definitions.text: What's the point of some animals?

parts.words: What's the point of some animals?
parts.note: the question seems to ask about the purpose of certain creatures, but means the pointed part of an elephant or walrus

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about why some creatures exist at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as purpose but means a sharp end: the long pointed tooth of an elephant, walrus or boar.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed tooth projecting from an elephant's mouth is literally its point.

clue.text: Choose a quiet spot

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a spot or place can be called a point

explanation.surface: Picking out a peaceful place.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to choose or name them for a role.

clue.text: Random glances could become source of gossip

indicators.note: says the letters of the two words could be reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: Casual looks at people might start rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who spreads scandal and rumour is a prime source of tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Strange patterns in part of church

indicators.note: strange signals the word patterns is made odd, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Unusual designs found in a section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross-arm of a cruciform church building.

clue.text: Grave message supported by queen that's more mature

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second, held up by it

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the inscription on a gravestone
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of a queen

explanation.surface: A queen backs a solemn epitaph for an older person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or people that have ripened further are comparatively more developed.

clue.text: Wrong men seen in empty tenement

indicators.note: says the second piece appears inside the first
an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the middle gone

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Mischief by men spotted in a deserted block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves T and T from tenement; 'seen in' puts OR between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong in law, one giving rise to a claim for damages.

clue.text: Being a swine, by the sound of it?

definitions.text: Being a swine, by the sound of it?

parts.words: Being a swine, by the sound of it?
parts.note: seems to mean behaving badly, judging by what one hears, but is the literal noise a pig makes

explanation.surface: Someone acting nastily, judging by the noises they make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' suggests a horrible person, but the answer is the grunting noise of an actual pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's grunting call is the noise one would make if literally a swine.

clue.text: Sent matter for analysis to find cures

indicators.note: material broken down for analysis is pulled apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Samples sent to a lab to find remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical therapies applied to patients are remedies, ways of curing illness.

clue.text: Criticise pianist's somewhat dark tone

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A critic finds the pianist's playing rather gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, as in old photographs, a dark shade.

clue.text: Scotsman caught wearing tech firm's device

indicators.note: the firm's name is worn around the Scotsman and caught, enclosing them

parts.note: Apple is the computer and phone company
Ian is the stock Scottish man's name in crosswords
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Scot is caught wearing a gadget made by a tech company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as dressed in, but signals one piece going round the others; the firm's name splits after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a machine or gadget, such as a kitchen device.

clue.text: Unusually poor gent aimed to become cheerful

indicators.note: unusually signals the words are set out in an odd order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A down-and-out man surprisingly sets out to look happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a good mood or humour is the idiom for being cheerful.

clue.text: Manufacturer regularly signed American apprentice

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of signed, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a trialist is someone on trial, a newcomer being tested

explanation.surface: A factory owner duly takes on an American trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrialist owns or runs factories, so is a maker of goods.

clue.text: Lag first to find completely live deer

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of find

parts.note: all means wholly or completely
to be is to exist or live
a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: A slowpoke is the first to spot a living deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail or drop back behind others is to lag.

clue.text: Beast bound to appear after intermittent rain at sea

indicators.note: the leaping word comes after the picked letters
intermittent picks every other letter, here the even ones of the three words

parts.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: An animal leaps after spells of rain at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittent' picks A, N, T, E from 'rain at sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a graceful hoofed animal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Married rogue in trouble remains here

parts.note: m is the genealogical abbreviation for married

indicators.note: a rogue in trouble is disturbed, so its letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A wedded scoundrel in difficulty stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' is a noun, a corpse, not the verb 'stays'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary is where dead bodies, a person's remains, are kept.

clue.text: Streaky bacon on top with rind already oddly missing

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top of bacon is its first letter
the odd letters are dropped, leaving the even ones of already

explanation.surface: Streaky bacon on top of the stack, its rind already partly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly missing' leaves L, E, D from already.
explanation.definitionFit: A brindled animal has streaks or patches of darker colour on its coat.

clue.text: Reader who may vote, being 27

indicators.note: 27-across means without a leader, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: an elector is a person entitled to vote

explanation.surface: A reader eligible to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 27-across is LEADERLESS, so the voter loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lector reads lessons aloud in church, or lectures at a university.

clue.text: Song drunk plays in company

indicators.note: puts the mixed letters inside the company abbreviation
drunk suggests the word plays reels about, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A tipsy song performed in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives ALYPS; 'in' sets it between the two letters of the business abbreviation. 'plays' looks like a verb about performing but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean song style from Trinidad.

clue.text: Admit accepting end for bank

indicators.note: the first word takes in the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to grant a point is to admit it
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Conceding a closing of the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a slope, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, and a bank is a sloping rise of ground.

clue.text: Agreement of new number during summer in France

indicators.note: places the new number within the French summer

parts.note: été is French for summer
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A new figure agreed in a French summer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, a diplomatic pact.

clue.text: Understanding to reduce the weight of chaps admitted by hospital department

indicators.note: the pieces are let into the hospital department, so they sit within it

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
to lighten a load is to make it less heavy
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A slimming programme for men run by a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlightenment is insight or knowledge, a state of clear comprehension.

clue.text: Rubbish outing supported by European

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece rests on the second

parts.note: a trip is an excursion or outing

explanation.surface: A worthless excursion backed by Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cow stomach, and figuratively nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Unchanged part of Christmas Island

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of an Indian Ocean territory left untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in its current state is the idiom for something unaltered.

clue.text: Just tell one student to hide answer

parts.note: to impart news is to tell it

indicators.note: the one and student wrap round the answer, concealing it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the learner plate for a student driver

explanation.surface: Simply tell a pupil to conceal the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is the adjective fair, not the adverb simply.
explanation.definitionFit: A just judgement is fair and even-handed, showing no bias.

clue.text: Criticise tourists on vacation? Rubbish!

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: vacated, the word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Knocking holidaymakers abroad: what a load of nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: PANTS is British slang for rubbish, as well as underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses pants as an exclamation meaning nonsense or poor quality.

clue.text: Physician to ignore court opening

indicators.note: ignoring the court leaves it out of the physician

parts.note: a physician is a medical doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor told to disregard the start of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' is a noun, an entrance, not a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is an entrance, an opening into a room or building.

clue.text: Lacking guidance, Liberal released criminal before start of sentence

indicators.note: places the earlier pieces ahead of the final letter
criminal suggests the word released is crooked, so its letters are reworked
takes the opening letter of sentence

explanation.surface: A Liberal frees a convict before he begins his jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: Without anyone in charge, a group has no direction or guiding head.
